### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 70dae533c58a60a7009d253cf73f87c3a5848d95` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3a129916f67e4877849e656a043540b75b65c039` — the merge of head `704a58ab232e0c7afe425b5df41518cd4151e3a5` into base `70dae533c58a60a7009d253cf73f87c3a5848d95`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a129916f67e4877849e656a043540b75b65c039 && git checkout 3a129916f67e4877849e656a043540b75b65c039
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 70dae533c58a60a7009d253cf73f87c3a5848d95 704a58ab232e0c7afe425b5df41518cd4151e3a5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 70dae533c58a60a7009d253cf73f87c3a5848d95 && git merge --no-ff 704a58ab232e0c7afe425b5df41518cd4151e3a5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 70dae533c58a60a7009d253cf73f87c3a5848d95
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `704a58ab232e0c7afe425b5df41518cd4151e3a5`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #20981 (body; comments 5923295010, 5926372178, 5927784503, 5929772241, 5929818992), PR #21157 (body, the 6-file list, the net diff from merge-base `e952cff57` of `origin/main`), and the 31 check-runs on the head. Read-only throughout: git fetch, diff, show and grep against the review ref, plus REST reads; nothing built, run or re-run.

1. **One-time gate, both positions, every depth — right.** `assertConditionIsEvaluable` throws `nonBooleanFlagComparandError` for `$exists` / `$null` when `typeof target` is not boolean, placed after the `$empty` gate and before the vocabulary check and the reference-position check. It is reached only through `assertNodeIsEvaluable`, which recurses every `$and` / `$or` branch and `$not`, so a branch the per-row `$or` would short-circuit past is judged. `assertHavingIsEvaluable` and `assertAggregationFilterIsEvaluable` both take that walk; `engine.aggregate` (untouched) calls the second in its per-aggregation loop, unconditionally, before `getDriver`, and the first once at the `having` seam before either `applyHaving` door is chosen. The refusal therefore precedes any driver read on the native and the rows path alike, and an empty table refuses too.

2. **Per-row floor and the two arms — right.** In `checkCondition` the same gate sits beside `$empty`'s, above the no-value exit (both flags are in `NO_VALUE_ANSWERED_BY_OPERATOR`, so an absent column still reaches the arm). The arms now compare the boolean itself: `$exists` keeps a row iff has-a-value equals `target`; `$null` keeps it iff has-no-value equals `target`. No `!!target`, and no `=== true` / `=== false` pair that let a third value through. `true` / `false` keep their prior semantics.

3. **The published `applyInMemoryAggregation(rows, ast, tz, fields)` — right, and named.** It runs no one-time flag walk (it never did for `$empty`; the only filter-level door it runs is #21007's JSON-column one), so for these flags it refuses per row through `matchesAggregationFilter` and `checkCondition`: a row that reaches the flag is refused, with or without `fields`; an empty `rows` array, or a row a `$or` branch settles first, is not judged there. That is the `$empty` precedent on `main`, consistent, and the changeset's BREAKING paragraph states exactly this reach. One phrase in the PR body ("both already route through the walker") is loose for this file — it routes through the per-row walk, not the one-time walker — but the changeset and the report are precise, and the new objectql file pins `applyInMemoryAggregation` with `fields`, `applyHaving` and `matchesAggregationFilter` on this.

4. **The declared verbatim copy — byte-equal, read side by side.** driver-sql's `nonBooleanExistsComparandError` / `nonBooleanNullComparandError` (sql-driver.ts) and the engine's `nonBooleanFlagComparandError` differ only where driver-sql writes "this driver" / "this driver's" and the engine writes "driver-sql" / "driver-sql's" (one occurrence per sentence), and in the location path. `describeFlagOperand` reproduces `describeFilterOperand` (null, array, typeof, constructor name unless Object) and `safeShapePreview` (JSON.stringify, typeof fallback, the 80-character cut at 77 plus "...") in the drivers' `kind (preview)` form. The copy is declared in its docblock, as the seat's amended fence requires.

5. **The equality pin can fail.** The rest cell reads `withheldFilterDiagnosticOf(err)` — the diagnostic driver-sql stores verbatim under its symbol, exported from `@objectstack/driver-sql`, a workspace dependency of `packages/rest` — asserts the twin's path is `filter.name.OP`, then requires `toBe` equality after exactly two edits (re-root the path; replaceAll "this driver" with "driver-sql"). A byte moved on either side, a twin not refused `INVALID_FILTER`, or a diagnostic no longer withheld each break it.

6. **Precedence — right.** A `{ $field }` under `$exists` / `$null` now meets the flag gate before `fieldReferencePositionError`; same code and status. The two pre-existing `REFERENCE_REFUSED` rows (engine-aggregate-filter.test.ts, engine-aggregate-having-comparand-shape.test.ts) assert `toContain(path)` only, so they stay green; the diff adds a pointer comment to each. An array in the slot, formerly answered by `!!target`, is now refused; a plain object or `undefined` keeps the comparand-type door's earlier words, as the PR says.

7. **Public surface.** No export, signature or published type moves; `index.ts`, `engine.ts`, `in-memory-aggregation.ts`, every driver, the spec and formula are outside the diff; `emptyFlagComparandError` is untouched. The rest test file is the claim's declared `domain:cli` test-only touch.

8. **The spec's three "every query face" sentences — true without a spec edit.** formula's `matchesFilterCondition` keeps its `v === true` reading, and its own docblock (matches-filter.ts, the `$empty` arm) contrasts itself with "the spec's save door and every query face", so after this fix the sentences hold for the query faces. The card offered "name it, or narrow the sentence"; the PR names it in its acceptance notes.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, with the BREAKING banner, the what-to-write-instead prose, and `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` in both the PR body and the changeset — the line the claim declared. Right: nothing new is accepted; shapes answered before are refused `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 now, and `true` / `false` answer as before. A narrowing is BREAKING and ships `minor` in the launch window (check-changeset-no-major.mjs; ADR-0087's level amendment). ADR-0087 marker: not-required (already-registered filter-query-face-comparands-refused-at-save). The entry pre-dates the merge base (present and registered at `e952cff57`); its surface names "the data-engine aggregate call's having, an aggregation filter", its reason states that every query face refuses a non-boolean `$null` / `$exists`, and its replacement is the boolean spelling this change prescribes — so it covers this migration rather than merely resolving. Only objectql publishes a change; the rest file is test-only. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0] (where the sentence lives):** answered in-seat, C (5929818992), with the claim's fence amended to one declared, equality-pinned copy. The diff is judged against that answer and matches it (①4, ①5). Not re-answered here.
- **Breach note (the claim said "REST cell"):** measured and right. `FindDataRequestSchema.query` is `QueryWithTransportSchema`, whose `having` and `aggregations[i].filter` are `FilterConditionSchema` with the #20116 superRefine, so the route refuses all three positions 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` before `engine.aggregate` is reached; the rest cell pins that in one case and drives the refusal cases through `engine.aggregate` over a real `SqlDriver` on SQLite — the pin the claim actually named ("through engine.aggregate ... on driver-sql"). The `true` / `false` control runs through the route.
- **driver-memory pin:** substituted by the engine-level rows-shape recorder, with the measurement table taken on the real `InMemoryDriver` (scratch, not committed), because driver-memory's test consumers are a closed census (`check:driver-memory-census`, root package.json) — the #20873 / #21007 precedent. Named in the report and in the file header; the refusal precedes every driver read, so the backend does not enter the verdict. Accepted as declared.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0] (turbo 2.11.5 writes an agent-guidance block into AGENTS.md):** not in this diff — AGENTS.md is absent from the file list. Escalated to the seat to route; nothing for this record to judge.
- **out_of_scope_findings[1] (formula still reads a non-boolean flag):** observation, verified (①8); no public door measured, not filed, not this card's.
- **out_of_scope_findings[2] (this face's `$empty` wording differs from the drivers'):** observation; `emptyFlagComparandError` is untouched here; the seat may carry it into the acceptance notes.

Skipped: Build Docs; Console Pin Gate; Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in). Still `in_progress`, so NOT verdicts here: Build Core; Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (5/6), (6/6); Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates; Lint & Repo Gates; Dogfood Regression Gate (2/3) and (3/3); Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL). The 39 objectql cases and the 15-case rest cell (the equality pin included) conclude inside Test Core; this record does not wait on them, and the queue lands only on their own conclusions.
